interest: This document provides a concise administrative record reflecting State Department tracking of interwar Japanese social and labor reform. Specifically, it notes the implementation of Japan's Child Welfare Law in October 1933 aimed at protecting children from exploitation as wage-earners. It is also useful for researchers tracing State Department records, illustrating how diplomatic dispatches were indexed, summarized on Form DS-46, and cross-referenced to related decimal files (such as 894.4055).
overview: This file contains a single Department of State List of Papers sheet (Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.5047, categorized under 'Child Labor --- Japan.' The docket sheet records an entry for Tokyo Despatch No. 702 sent by Arthur Garrels to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE) on October 6, 1933. The entry summarizes the salient features of Japan's new Child Welfare Law, which took effect on October 1, 1933, to protect children from persecution and various forms of wage-earning exploitation, while directing researchers to cross-reference file 894.4055.

subfiles.summary: This document is a Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) for subject 'Child Labor --- Japan' under decimal file 894.5047. It indexes Despatch No. 702 dated October 6, 1933, from Tokyo (Garrels) to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE). The docket entry notes the enactment on October 1, 1933, of Japan's Child Welfare Law protecting children from exploitation and persecution as wage-earners, and references decimal file 894.4055.
